create an email resopnse to this: B2B Market Expansion Strategy
The team agreed to focus on expanding into the B2B market to scale the new course efficiently and tap into larger client bases beyond individual med spa owners.

Bethany Gifford outlined a plan to generate a minimum of 20 qualified new B2B client opportunities within 90 days by targeting larger med spas, franchises, device vendors, and aesthetic schools rather than individual owners (08:31)

The strategy relies on identifying multiple buyer personas within the B2B ecosystem to maximize reach and adoption.
This approach aims to leverage big players who can promote the course to their network, creating organic growth across smaller clients.
Bethany stressed that this B2B angle is a conservative estimate given the course’s newness but offers a scalable growth path.
Jodi Mehlenbacher confirmed alignment with this strategy, emphasizing complementarity to their current marketing efforts.
Bethany emphasized the necessity of specialized market intelligence and targeted outreach using AI-driven data tools to identify and engage the right B2B prospects effectively (15:46)

This intelligence addresses inefficiencies in outreach by pinpointing ideal partners and reducing wasted spend.
The team’s competitive edge lies in combining marketing and strategic consulting, allowing responsive pivoting beyond traditional agencies.
Bethany’s agency currently manages about 15 clients monthly across aesthetics and wellness, validating their experience with similar B2B targeting.
Jodi appreciated the data-backed approach and expressed interest in further testing pricing and messaging.
Course Launch and Growth Phases
The launch plan emphasizes gradual growth with scalable automation and handholding initially, transitioning into streamlined AI support as volume increases.

Bethany proposed a phased rollout beginning with personal engagement and manual outreach, progressing to AI-driven automation as volume grows to handle inquiries and qualifying leads without increasing headcount excessively (17:11)

Paige, the practice manager, will manage initial inbound calls and qualifying conversations, leveraging her deep course knowledge.
The AI assistant will eventually replicate Paige’s expertise to answer common student questions, supporting scale beyond hundreds of users.
This staged approach balances personalized service with operational efficiency to maintain quality while growing.
Bethany noted the importance of keeping the process human-like to avoid alienating prospects.
The plan includes ongoing optimization and pivoting based on ROI metrics and market feedback over 3 to 6 months to refine targeting, messaging, and delivery (20:49)

Bethany guaranteed a minimum of 20 qualified leads within 90 days or her team would work for free until hitting that benchmark.
She highlighted the importance of evolving the approach after gathering case studies, testimonials, and user data.
The 6-month horizon aims to reach a point where the course can be aggressively marketed with less hands-on support.
This incremental model reduces upfront risk and aligns investment with measurable progress.
Financial Model and Pricing Validation
The meeting clarified investment expectations and revenue-sharing terms, emphasizing cost-effectiveness and alignment with business realities.

The initial investment includes a $7,000 upfront fee and ongoing monthly payments, with a revenue-sharing model of 10% on sales generated from the B2B partnerships (32:58)

Bethany detailed that the 10% applies only to revenue from clients her team brings in, not total company revenue.
Jodi noted that the upfront costs approximate prior ad spends of about $25,000 over 3 months but are spread out with added B2B targeting value.
Bethany assured the investment pays for setup, AI system integration, CRM customization, and campaign management.
The revenue share is negotiable depending on partnership scale and longevity.
Pricing for course packages was reviewed, with the master course at $2,500 and launch course at $1,999, considered competitive and accessible by industry standards (36:06)

Bethany’s market research found no comparable comprehensive med spa business courses, giving the product a strong competitive edge.
She stressed the price point aligns well with the value of a million-dollar business education and is lower than many specialized workshops.
Future pricing adjustments will be tested based on customer feedback and market response.
Jodi confirmed willingness to adapt messaging and content to optimize conversion.
Integration with Existing Marketing and Operations
The strategy complements the current direct-to-consumer marketing efforts and existing course content while preparing for future scale.

Bethany acknowledged the client’s current DIY marketing strengths but identified opportunities to boost authority and positioning in the B2B space (11:53)

She noted the importance of building an authoritative presence early to stand out in a competitive and fast-growing med spa market.
The plan includes auditing existing ads and providing feedback on scripts and promotional content to improve effectiveness.
Bethany suggested the B2B launch would provide steady qualified leads that the team can convert with personal follow-up.
Jodi confirmed Paige’s role in managing incoming B2B inquiries to ensure smooth handoff and qualification.
The course launch is intended to feed revenue growth that supports scaling the med spa business itself, including future locations or expanded services (45:14)

Bethany emphasized that strong course sales and market presence will enhance the med spa’s brand credibility and attract more clients.
She recommended keeping focus on the course now while planning for operational capacity to handle growth later.
The phased approach ensures the business can absorb new demand without sacrificing quality or overextending resources.
Jodi agreed that marketing efforts should align with the med spa’s capacity and readiness to onboard new clients.
Partnership Framework and Next Steps
There is agreement to formalize the partnership with clear contracts and timelines, with a follow-up meeting scheduled to review details.

Bethany committed to sending a detailed proposal and partnership agreement outlining fees, revenue shares, deliverables, and timelines for review (39:36)

The agreement will clarify expectations and structure to protect all parties and ensure accountability.
Jodi requested the documents to enable internal analysis and financial modeling before making a decision.
Both parties agreed to reconvene in approximately two weeks on Wednesday the 29th to discuss feedback and next steps.
Bethany assured ongoing availability for questions and collaboration to keep momentum moving forward.
The partnership is intended to be dynamic, with flexibility to pivot strategies based on early performance and market feedback (48:14)

Bethany highlighted that this initial B2B launch is one piece of a broader growth vision that will evolve with data.
The model supports scaling from 20 qualified leads to hundreds or thousands as operational capacity and marketing sophistication increase.
This approach balances risk and reward while building a sustainable foundation for long-term success.
Jodi expressed confidence in the plan’s potential but acknowledged the unknowns inherent in launching a new course.

Action items
Jodi Mehlenbacher
Review the detailed proposal and metrics shared by Bethany and collaborate with team to crunch numbers for budget and viability (39:36)
Coordinate brainstorming internally to evaluate the presented growth plan and possible counteroffers (49:30)
Confirm and prepare for follow-up meeting on March 29th at 10:30 AM Eastern (50:30)
Communicate review feedback and any additional questions or ideas to Bethany via email or text (51:10)
Bethany Gifford
Send the detailed presentation, proposal, and metrics to Jodi for review (49:30)
Prepare and finalize partnership agreement for Thrive Wellness Academy’s review (39:36)
Provide case studies and additional research on comparable B2B strategies and educational programs (29:10)
Coordinate internally to support the launch and scale efforts including AI automation, lead targeting, and marketing campaign setup (00:00)

Subject: Thrive Wellness Academy B2B Launch — recap, materials, and next steps

Hi Jodi,

Great meeting. I am excited about the B2B expansion plan for the course and I appreciate the alignment on targeting larger med spas, franchises, device vendors, and aesthetic schools.

Quick recap  
• Goal, a minimum of 20 qualified B2B opportunities in 90 days, targeting multiple buyer personas to drive network effects.  
• Rollout, start with personal outreach and handholding, then scale with AI for inquiries and qualification as volume grows.  
• Operations, Paige to manage early inbound and qualification, the AI assistant will mirror her knowledge for scale.  
• Investment model, 7,000 dollars upfront for setup and integration, plus 10 percent revenue share on sales we source through B2B partnerships.  
• Guarantee, if we do not deliver 20 qualified opportunities within 90 days, my team will work at no cost until we reach that benchmark.  
• Pricing, current course pricing of 2,500 dollars for the master course and 1,999 dollars for the launch course remains competitive while we test messaging.

What I will send today  
1) Presentation deck and metrics summary  
2) Detailed proposal with deliverables, timeline, and the 90-day guarantee language  
3) Partnership agreement draft outlining fees, revenue share, and scope  
4) Case studies and comparable B2B program research, focused on authority building and multi-persona outreach

What I need from your side  
• Internal review of the proposal and numbers, including any counteroffers you want me to model  
• Notes on messaging and pricing tests you would like us to run first  
• Confirmation on roles, Paige as first-line qualifier and any additional team members we should loop into enablement

Meeting and timing  
I have our follow-up penciled in for Wednesday, October 29 at 10:30 AM Eastern. If that timing needs to move, please share a couple of alternates and I will adjust.

Focus for the next 2 weeks  
• Build the B2B target map, franchises, device vendors, aesthetic schools, multi-location groups  
• Draft tailored outreach sequences by persona, owner, operator, education director, vendor partner  
• Prepare the first authority assets, short proof videos, one-pager, offer sheet, FAQ drawn from Paige’s call notes  
• Set up tracking, CRM views, AI assistant knowledge base outline, and qualification definitions so reporting is clean from day one

Thank you again for the thoughtful discussion. Once you have reviewed the materials, send any questions or redlines and I will turn revisions quickly so we can keep momentum.

Best,  
Bethany Gifford  
New Era Intel  
bethany@neweraintel.com | 555-555-5555

Subject: Follow-up: B2B Market Expansion Plan  

Hi Jodi,  

Thanks again for the great conversation. I’m really encouraged by the alignment on the B2B direction and appreciate your openness to building this next phase together.  

I’ll send over a short proposal and partnership outline today that includes the key deliverables, timeline, and performance guarantee. Once you’ve had time to review internally, we can connect on the 29th to finalize details and next steps.  

This approach has a lot of potential to open new doors quickly, and I’m confident we can make strong traction in the first 90 days.  

Talk soon,  
Bethany  

Bethany Gifford  
New Era Intel
